title: In v2 size canvases and compute screen centres from clientWidth, never innerWidth or a transformed getBoundingClientRect
body: v2.css sets html { scrollbar-gutter: stable } so that holdScroll's is-held overflow hiding shifts nothing. As a result innerWidth includes the gutter (e.g. 2560 against a 2545 px page). A fixed canvas sized from innerWidth squeezes every point left, more the further right it is: the morph's points missed their seats this way. Size backing stores from the canvas's own clientWidth/clientHeight and take the screen centre from document.documentElement.clientWidth (ghostCenter in peak.ts, the caret in seats.ts). Second trap: the map's canvas sits inside a 3D-tilted element. Sizing it from getBoundingClientRect() reads the PROJECTED box, so a rebuild mid-tilt (on resize) got a squashed height and cut off the bottom of the map. Size it from clientWidth/clientHeight (map.ts). A rect is still the right tool for reading where something is ON SCREEN (the .peak__probe points in morph.ts).
not_derivable: The reason is spread over one-line comments in four files; new canvas or centring code would naturally reach for innerWidth or a rect.

evidence.summary: html { scrollbar-gutter: stable } next to the is-held rules
canvas sized from clientWidth/clientHeight, not the transformed rect
